newsitem.title: FALKLAND ISLANDS: Falklands oil company won't pay Argentine royalty.
newsitem.headline: Falklands oil company won't pay Argentine royalty.

text.p: The chairman of one of the companies granted licences to explore for oil off the Falkland Islands said on Saturday his company would not pay a three percent royalty fee requested by the Argentine government.
Colin Phipps, chairman of Desire Petroleum, told reporters during a visit to the disputed islands:
"I don't think there is any question that Desire will pay three percent royalty to the Argentine government as Desire Petroleum has no activities whatever in Argentina.
"We are a British company which is exploring in a British colony in the Falkland Islands," Phipps said.

The Falkland Islands government issued licences in October to 13 companies operating in seven different tranches in waters north of the islands. Desire won tranches I and L and is part of a consortium with British independent company Lasmo for tranches C and D.
Seismic surveying is expected to begin in January 1997 and drilling could start as soon as October or November next year.

Argentina, which fought a bloody 10-week war war with Britain in 1982 over the Falklands, has insisted that all companies licensed to prospect for oil around the islands should be required to make a three percent royalty payment when production starts.
The Buenos Aires government claims sovereignty over the waters around the islands, which it calls the Malvinas, but Britain has refused to discuss the issue.
Estimates vary as to the amount of oil lying off the Falklands but industry analysts believe there may be two to three billion barrels there.
